title: Agent brain: who takes each step

flows.name: Commit a change
flows.summary: P1–P4: a small working commit with the ticket id and the model, effort and harness it was made with.
steps: Slice the change into one coherent capability
Write the subject, the why, and the summary
Subject shape, ticket id, and the Model / Thinking-effort / Harness trailers
Install the commit-msg and pre-push hooks

flows.name: Branch and worktree
flows.summary: P5–P7 and DS2–DS3: one branch and one sibling worktree per ticket.
steps: Create the sibling worktree, agent name, lowercase Compose project, free ports
Remove the worktree after the PR is open
Delete the local and remote branch after merge

flows.name: Raise a pull request
flows.summary: P8, P10, P11, P13: one PR per ticket, small, with a changelog line.
steps: Find the existing PR for the ticket before creating one
A CHANGELOG.md line is in the change
Fill the PR body from the template
Decide how to split an oversized change
Request the reviewer and link the PR on the ticket

flows.name: Review a pull request
flows.summary: P10, P14: adversarial review with inline findings and a submitted verdict.
steps: Rate each finding's severity and propose the fix
Post inline comments and a submitted verdict
File a review issue in Linear per finding
Author fixes, replies with the commit, resolves the thread
Read the PR's CI status and act on it

flows.name: Merge a pull request
flows.summary: P12, P15: a merge commit with the ticket id, only when green and approved.
steps: CI green and review approved (or review optional on the ticket)
Merge commit, never squash, ticket id in the message
Move the ticket to Merged with a status update

flows.name: Release a version
flows.summary: L1: semver, a changelog entry listing the tickets, a tag and a GitHub release.
steps: Pick the semver bump from the change's consumer impact
Write the changelog entry from the merged tickets
Tag vX.Y.Z and publish the release
Decide that the release should go out

flows.name: Take in a request
flows.summary: M1–M2: the request lands in Triage verbatim, then is classified.
steps: Record the prompt verbatim on a Triage issue
Classify kind, owning persona, scope, and size

flows.name: Move an issue and say why
flows.summary: M3, M5: every state change carries a structured status update.
steps: Is the move legal, and which states does it skip
Render the status update in the template's shape
Validate the Blocked block and its blocker type
Write the reason, evidence, and next action
Post the comment and change the state in Linear
Read back and quote the identifier

flows.name: Set up a team's workflow
flows.summary: Created once per team by the user.
steps: Create the missing workflow states in order

flows.name: Plan the work
flows.summary: Scope, milestones, issues, estimates, cycles.
steps: Decide scope and divide it into milestones and issues
Estimate effort on the team's scale
Create the project, milestones, issues, and relations
Review the plan and the PRD

flows.name: Write a PRD
flows.summary: Idea to a phased PRD with an MVP first.
steps: Interview the user and refine the idea

flows.name: Write HLD, LLD and ADRs
flows.summary: Design as code, reviewed by the user.
steps: Decide the architecture and the contracts
Write the HLD, LLD, and ADRs
Documents sit where W9–W11 say and are in the index
Rendered HTML sits beside its Markdown

flows.name: Implement a slice
flows.summary: Code and tests in the agent's own environment, one verified behavior per commit.
steps: Design the code and write it
Write the test behind each acceptance criterion
Run lint, type check, tests, and build
Start the service in its own Docker project and seed data

flows.name: Hold the coding standards
flows.summary: C1–C23 split into what a linter can see and what needs a reader.
steps: Strict types, no any, linter and type checker present
No edits to generated or vendor files
No inline clock or randomness in business modules
No secrets in source or fixtures
Separate API, domain, and DB models; errors as domain objects
Business validation only at the edges

flows.name: Debug a failure
flows.summary: Reproduce, localise, fix, guard.
steps: Localise the cause and choose the fix

flows.name: Audit security
flows.summary: Never holds a PR (P9).
steps: Scan for secrets and vulnerable dependencies
Reason about trust boundaries and abuse cases

flows.name: Audit web performance
flows.summary: Measured numbers only.

flows.name: Verify a milestone
flows.summary: Independent end-to-end and concurrency verification.
steps: Design the end-to-end and race scenarios
File a bug issue per failure

flows.name: Double-pass review of a brain PR
flows.summary: AGENTS.md gate: two independent reviewers, then a synthesis.
steps: Start both reviewers on the same revision with fixed models
Check that both reviews and the synthesis cover the final revision

flows.name: Start a session
flows.summary: /brain: one persona, declared.
steps: Pick a persona for the task
Fetch the skills its table names for the activity
Declare persona, skills, tools, model, harness, effort

flows.name: Check the brain
flows.summary: Anatomies, links, commands, evals, and the persona table.
steps: Persona anatomy, manifest, and the persona table

flows.name: Build and install the brain
flows.summary: manifest.json to build/ to a project.
steps: Pull the brain into a repository
Decide which skills and personas the brain contains

flows.name: Turn a learning into a rule
flows.summary: LEARNINGS.md notes become changes here.
steps: Record the override, correction, or gap when it happens
Decide that a note recurs enough to change a rule
Approve the change to the brain

flows.name: Session hooks
flows.summary: Hooks that run without a model.
steps: Inject the meta-skill at session start (the hook script exists but no host registers it)
Cache source reads before and after

flows.name: Run a dev machine
flows.summary: EC2 Spot machines for developers.
steps: Survive a Spot reclaim and relaunch

flows.name: Build iOS on EAS
flows.summary: DS16: only with explicit permission.
steps: Count free builds, queue, build, report
Decide to wait or build elsewhere when the budget is spent

flows.name: Instrument what ships
flows.summary: O1–O8: structured logs and RED metrics for every new boundary.
steps: Decide which metrics and log events matter
Bounded labels and no PII or secrets in logs
Provision dashboards and alerts at the planned milestone
